claims.text: Direct Lake loads column data from OneLake lazily: nothing is read until a query first touches a column, and the load set includes not just columns the query names but also those needed by relationships and measures.

A resident column can be evicted for three reasons: a refresh (framing) after the source Delta table changed, prolonged non-use by queries, or general memory pressure on the capacity from concurrent operations.

Framing is a metadata-only refresh that typically finishes in seconds: the model reads the latest Delta table version and rebinds itself to the current Parquet file set, establishing the new baseline for future transcoding.
Direct Lake queries reflect the Delta table state as of the most recent successful framing operation, not the live table, so writes landing after the last frame remain invisible until the next one.

Pinning queries to a framing point is useful when Delta data is transient (for example mid-ETL): disabling automatic updates and framing deliberately yields consistent results during long-running loads.
Framing can fail when a Delta table breaches capacity guardrails, such as exceeding 10,000 Parquet files in a single table.

An automatic-updates model setting, on by default, reframes Direct Lake tables whenever the underlying OneLake data changes; turn it off to control data visibility through manual or scheduled framing.

DirectQuery fallback exists only in Direct Lake on SQL; documented triggers are querying a SQL-endpoint view, querying a table with SQL-endpoint row-level security, and a Delta table exceeding capacity guardrails.
A fallen-back query reads the SQL analytics endpoint directly and therefore returns the latest data, escaping the framing point-in-time — at the cost of typically slower performance.
Direct Lake on OneLake never falls back to DirectQuery and skips SQL-endpoint coupling entirely, which enables more efficient DAX query plans since no SQL security check is needed.
Fallback behavior for Direct Lake on SQL models is governed by the model's DirectLakeBehavior property; the property has no effect on Direct Lake on OneLake models.
The Fabric capacity SKU sets the maximum memory available to each Direct Lake semantic model, which bounds how much column data can be resident at once.
